Selective in One’s Opportunities: Cambridge Associates’ Keirsten Lawton recently told me about the rise of independent sponsors becoming a major part of the lower-middle market. Read my full article here.

Independent sponsors are investors who make deals one-by-one rather than through the construct of a fund. The idea is to target individual companies with roughly $5 million in EBITDA that don’t have a succession plan and are too small to get noticed by the big players. This is private equity, different from angel investing where an investor seeds a bunch of venture startups in the hope that some will take off. These are deals in which the sponsor is a controlling owner of the holding.
